c.tagline: Venetian old town, twin fortresses, and the Ionian's greenest island.

taxi.fareNote: Ride-hailing apps like Uber and Bolt are effectively unavailable on Corfu; you hail metered taxis at ranks or phone/radio-book them. Confirm the fare or zone tariff for out-of-town trips, and expect a 25-30% surcharge for late-night rides.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance, with English-speaking operators.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Kavos and other party resorts see alcohol-fuelled trouble at night, and Corfu Town's crowded lanes draw occasional pickpockets in high season.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed Venetian heart of Corfu Town, a maze of narrow kantounia (alleys), the arcaded Liston, Spianada square and the two fortresses; best for first-timers who want history, cafes, and sights on foot.

A scenic seaside neighborhood just south of the Old Town with a 2 km promenade from the Old Fortress to the Windmill, leafy parkland and some of the island's finest tavernas; a peaceful, villagey base with an authentic local feel.

The green, lush peninsula south of town, once the island's original capital, famed for the view over Mouse Island (Pontikonisi) and the Vlacherna monastery; a calm area of mid-sized resort hotels close to the airport.

Corfu Town's working port district north of the center, home to the ferry harbor, budget rooms and lively local tavernas and bars; handy for early ferries and travelers wanting an unpolished, affordable base.
A relaxed coastal suburb north of town with a yacht marina, small beaches and family resorts, linked to the center by frequent blue buses; good for a quieter, greener stay with easy town access.

water.note: Tap water quality varies around the island; most visitors drink bottled.

transit.hours: Blue town buses run roughly 6:00am to 10:00-11:00pm; green intercity buses run mostly daytime with sparse evening service, so late nights rely on taxis.
transit.note: Corfu has no metro, tram or rail. Two bus networks cover the island: blue urban buses around Corfu Town and its suburbs, and green KTEL coaches to the rest of the island.
transit.pay: Pay the driver or conductor in cash on board. Blue urban buses around Corfu Town cost roughly €1.20-1.70 a ride; the green KTEL intercity buses to island villages and resorts are priced by distance, bought at the bus station or on board. There is no contactless or rechargeable card system.

transit.m: Blue Bus line 15 to San Rocco Square / town (~10-15 min)
Taxi to Corfu Town center (~10 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated.
